text: so  ok when you say its soup, that doesnt really sound like a good thing and i cant imagine it really is,
resolution: Question-only ask, no code changed. Gave the honest assessment of 'triangle soup' (the non-indexed vertex stream): it is not a correctness or rendering-quality problem and was the right v1 — flat expanded faces are what make the host mesh editor's part ranges, face selection, paint, and journal simple, and hard-surface authored props need vertex splits at every crease anyway so their real duplication factor is ~2x, kilobytes in practice. Where it IS genuinely wasteful: smooth/dense geometry (imports, sculpts, cylinders) duplicates each shared vertex ~6x in memory AND runs the vertex shader per duplicate. The known fix is the indexed-mesh pipeline (already flagged at MAX_DYN_VERTS as the real long-term fix); recommended shape = keep authoring/editing on expanded faces, index at cook/intern time so cooked assets + the GPU copy are indexed while editor drafts stay soup — consistent with V29 (an index lump is still raw aligned data). Sized it as a real project (touches every 3D pipeline, intern cache, dyn slots) and offered to take it on; awaiting the user's word.
